text: Cache compressed summaries of subtrees, keyed by a content hash
description:
Inspired by HIPIF (arXiv 2606.10507) and Task-Decoupled Planning (2601.07577): fold completed sub-goals into short summaries, keep the active work raw. get_idea_context currently returns parents, children and 5 semantic neighbours in full. (Distinct from session-memory compression, 654b56f9, which compresses session summaries, not graph subtrees.)

Design thoughts:
- Key: Merkle-style hash(text, status, status comment, sorted child hashes). Not a dirty flag — git pull, branch switches, wrapped agents and manual edits change .bowman outside the backend. Stale summaries just miss the cache; multi-parent propagation is automatic. Store in cache.db (gitignored, derived data). Probably exclude value/cost/weights from the hash.
- Bottom-up: a parent's summary is built from its children's summaries, so a leaf change regenerates only its path(s) to the root.
- Two tiers: mechanical (status counts, open leaves, 'Lesson:' lines from status comments) — free, computed on read; LLM summary — cached, regenerated lazily, served stale with a marker.
- Mostly worth it for finished subtrees (stable → cache hits). get_idea_context: finished children as one cached line each, open children raw, open subtrees mechanical only.
- Who writes LLM summaries: not the working agent mid-task. Preferred: the supervisor/loop as idle work through a hash-checked set_summary(ideaId, hash, text) (rejected on hash mismatch). Later: MCP sampling if clients support it. Backend calling a model itself = new dependency.
- Caveats: summaries are text other agents read → on the hosted instance set_summary needs edit permission and authorship (injection vector). Wrong summaries persist until content changes → show node count and a regenerate action.

Open: use it for the graph view too (finished subtree as one collapsed node)? Is the mechanical tier alone enough?

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Folding finished children into one line keeps the context an agent reads proportional to the open work, without any cached summary.

status.comment: Felix (2026-10-17): liked the direction, no decision yet. Open: mechanical tier only vs. LLM tier written by the loop; agent context only or also the graph view.
